verdict.rationale: LlamaParse documents natural-language inputs within several of its own products. Classify accepts natural-language rules, Parse can be guided with custom prompts, and Extract can generate schemas from a prompt. Its hosted MCP endpoint also exposes Parse, Classify, Extract, Split and Index as tools for MCP clients. However, these are prompt-driven configuration of individual operations rather than a documented way to operate the product as a whole through natural-language commands. Missing for 10: a first-party natural-language command interface for operating the product overall, and independent or hands-on corroboration of natural-language operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Classify lets you automatically categorize documents into types you define (for example: invoice, receipt, contract) using natural-language rules.
Guide parsing output with custom prompts.
Generate extraction schemas with a prompt
exposes the platform's document processing — Parse, Classify, Extract, Split, and Index — as tools any MCP client can call
